1 فَحَسَ , aor.
فَحَسَ , inf. n. فَحْسٌ, He took a thing from his hand, with his tongue and his mouth; such as water &c.: (Lth, T, O, K:) or he licked up a thing with his tongue, from his hand. (O: but only the inf. n. is mentioned.) ―
-b2- And فَحَسَ السَّلْتَ, aor. as above, (O,) and so the inf. n., (O, K,) He rubbed [the ears off] the سلت, (O, K, TA,) a particular species of barley, (TA,) so that the awn, or beard, [thereof] became removed (O, K, TA) and scattered. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
